item.title: Topologically Obstructed Kondo Hybridization: A Route to Kondo Semimetals
item.description: arXiv:2611.26686v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The interplay of strong correlations, topology, and symmetry can reshape the low-energy electronic structure of quantum materials and drive the emergence of novel quantum phases. In heavy-fermion systems, the Kondo effect entangles …
item.itunes:summary: arXiv:2611.26686v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The interplay of strong correlations, topology, and symmetry can reshape the low-energy electronic structure of quantum materials and drive the emergence of novel quantum phases. In heavy-fermion systems, the Kondo effect entangles localized $f$ moments with conduction electrons, giving rise to coherent heavy-electron bands at low temperatures, typically characterized by a Kondo hybridization gap. Here we show, however, that the topology and symmetry of the conduction-electron Fermi surface can obstruct the opening of the Kondo hybridization gap at certain momenta. Treating the Fermi surface of a three-dimensional system as an effective two-dimensional manifold, we demonstrate that nontrivial topological invariants defined on this manifold impose a topological obstruction to opening a full hybridization gap, forcing the $fc$ hybridization to vanish at certain momenta on the Fermi surface. These hybridization zeros lead to crossings between $c$ and $f$ bands, giving rise to nodal points or lines near the Fermi energy within the Kondo phase. Our results establish topological obstructions to Kondo hybridization as a route to Kondo semimetals, revealing a fundamental connection between Fermi-surface topology and the emergence of correlated electronic phases.

item.title: Off-diagonal long-range order and $p$-wave pairing in one dimension from critical density fluctuations
item.description: arXiv:2611.26690v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A central theme in the theory of unconventional superconductivity is that Cooper pairing can be mediated by bosonic collective modes other than lattice vibrations. However, collective fluctuations in reduced dimensions can also have…
item.itunes:summary: arXiv:2611.26690v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A central theme in the theory of unconventional superconductivity is that Cooper pairing can be mediated by bosonic collective modes other than lattice vibrations. However, collective fluctuations in reduced dimensions can also have a destabilizing effect on superconductivity, by suppressing long-range order or by destroying Fermi-liquid quasiparticles in the normal state. In this work, we study a one-dimensional (1D) model of spinless fermions with local interactions that exhibits a continuous quantum phase transition from a Luttinger liquid to a phase-separated state. Combining field-theoretic arguments with numerical exact diagonalization and matrix-product-state methods, we find that the quantum critical point exhibits two-particle off-diagonal long-range order and $p$-wave pairing. Our work shows that critical density fluctuations at a phase-separation instability can act as pairing glue for unconventional superconductivity in 1D, overcoming the disordering effect of phase fluctuations and the absence of long-lived fermionic quasiparticles in the normal state.

item.title: Impact of spin fluctuations on spectral functions and transport in a model altermagnet
item.description: arXiv:2611.26725v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Understanding spin dependent transport in altermagnets is important for incorporating them in next generation spintronic technologies. Motivated by the discovery of altermagnetism in strongly correlated quantum materials, we explore…
item.itunes:summary: arXiv:2611.26725v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Understanding spin dependent transport in altermagnets is important for incorporating them in next generation spintronic technologies. Motivated by the discovery of altermagnetism in strongly correlated quantum materials, we explore this physics in the checkerboard lattice Hubbard model using a fermion Monte Carlo approach which tracks the full spatial dependence of spin fluctuations as a function of temperature. We present results for the evolution of the spin-dependent single particle spectral functions and transport as we go from the ordered ground state into the high temperature disordered paramagnetic phase. Our results could be tested in future spin-selective angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy (ARPES) and spin transport experiments in candidate altermagnets realized in solid state quantum materials or in proposed ultracold atomic systems.

item.title: Emergent Long-Range Entanglement in the XXZ Quantum Spin Chain with Competing Orders
item.description: arXiv:2611.26741v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Competition between short-range and long-range interactions is a largely unexplored route to one-dimensional quantum matter. We introduce a spin-1/2 XXZ chain with ferromagnetic nearest-neighbour and antiferromagnetic power-law coup…
item.itunes:summary: arXiv:2611.26741v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Competition between short-range and long-range interactions is a largely unexplored route to one-dimensional quantum matter. We introduce a spin-1/2 XXZ chain with ferromagnetic nearest-neighbour and antiferromagnetic power-law couplings. Using DMRG and spin-wave theory, we show this competition stabilises a gapless phase with central charge $c=0.997(17)$, a twofold-degenerate ground state and entanglement spectrum, absent in nearest-neighbour models, and is long-range entangled as diagnosed by finite quantum conditional mutual information. The model also generates a unique gapped quantum phase and gapless antiphase with non-decaying correlations.

item.title: Geometric Contribution to the Electron-Phonon Coupling Constant: Checkerboard and Hyper-diamond Models
item.description: arXiv:2611.26823v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Recent theoretical studies on electron-phonon coupling (EPC) - a key ingredient in the emergence of diverse quantum phases such as superconductivity and charge-density waves - have revealed a distinct contribution to its strength ar…
item.itunes:summary: arXiv:2611.26823v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Recent theoretical studies on electron-phonon coupling (EPC) - a key ingredient in the emergence of diverse quantum phases such as superconductivity and charge-density waves - have revealed a distinct contribution to its strength arising from the quantum geometry of electronic bands. Here we investigate the quantum geometric contribution, characterized by the quantum metric, to the dimensionless EPC constant in the checkerboard and hyper-diamond models, under the Gaussian approximation. We show that in the checkerboard model, the geometric contribution can be tuned independently while keeping the energetic part fixed, demonstrating the possibility of enhancing EPC strength through quantum geometry. In the hyper-diamond model, the geometric contribution accounts for roughly $50\%$ of the total EPC constant across all spatial dimensions, generalizing the $d=2$ result for graphene to higher dimensions.

item.title: Majorana quasiparticles, mass hierarchies, and the phase diagram of the Gross-Neveu model in D=2+1
item.description: arXiv:2611.26872v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We show that the canonical $2+1$-dimensional $O(2N)$-symmetric Gross-Neveu model with the inversion-breaking mass-term features a sequence of $O(2N-k) \times O(k)$ - symmetric ground states in its zero-temperature phase diagram, wit…
item.itunes:summary: arXiv:2611.26872v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We show that the canonical $2+1$-dimensional $O(2N)$-symmetric Gross-Neveu model with the inversion-breaking mass-term features a sequence of $O(2N-k) \times O(k)$ - symmetric ground states in its zero-temperature phase diagram, with $k=1,...,N$. For odd $k$ the quasiparticle excitations are itinerant, massive, two-real-component Majorana fermions, i.e. half of Dirac fermions. The solutions of the mean-field equations symmetric under $O(2N-k_1-k_2) \times O(k_1) \times O(k_2)$ with $k_1, k_2 \geq 1$ also exist, but are found to be unstable. Some manifestations of Majorana quasiparticle in the particular ``uniaxial nematic" state with $k=1$ are outlined, and analogies to other physical systems are offered.

item.title: Quantum order by disorder among lozenge tilings: a staircase of hub-free crystals between the Lieb ferrimagnet and the antiferromagnet
item.description: arXiv:2611.27076v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Lozenge tilings of the triangular lattice define an exponentially large family of bipartite networks, from the dice lattice, a Lieb ferrimagnet with the largest sublattice imbalance, to square-type tilings, which are compensated ant…
item.itunes:summary: arXiv:2611.27076v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Lozenge tilings of the triangular lattice define an exponentially large family of bipartite networks, from the dice lattice, a Lieb ferrimagnet with the largest sublattice imbalance, to square-type tilings, which are compensated antiferromagnets. For the classical Heisenberg antiferromagnet all of them are degenerate. We show that quantum fluctuations lift this degeneracy through a local mechanism: the zero-point energy is, to leading order, a sum of site terms that are convex in the coordination $z$, so that Jensen's inequality at fixed $\langle z\rangle=4$ selects the square-type tiling. An expansion about the Ising limit explains the convexity: a site with more bonds has more channels for quantum fluctuations, but each fluctuation frustrates more bonds. A magnetic field couples to the Lieb moment and competes with this selection. Because the moment is carried most cheaply by threefold and fivefold sites, sixfold hubs are avoided, and bond counting together with the Lieb--Mattis theorem limits hub-free tilings to $3/5$ of the dice moment. Quantum Monte Carlo and a complete enumeration of periodic tilings with small unit cells show that the classical jump is replaced by a staircase of periodic crystals. Its widest step is a hub-free crystal that saturates the bound; below it, threefold and fivefold defects pack ever more densely in a shallow sequence of crystals, controlled by a short-ranged attraction between defects of equal curvature and a repulsion between defects of opposite curvature. Selection energies scale as $JS$. In the height representation the coordination is the discrete Gaussian curvature and the Lieb moment its sublattice-staggered part. We give spectroscopic signatures and discuss realizations in nanographenes, atomic spin arrays and quantum simulators.

item.title: Kinetic Arrest of a Disordered First-Order Phase Transition in Strained V2O3 Thin Films
item.description: arXiv:2611.27168v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We develop a continuum phenomenological theory for the kinetic arrest (KA) of a first-order phase transition (FOPT), taking the thermal and electric field-driven metal-insulator transition (MIT) in epitaxial V2O3 thin films as a pro…
item.itunes:summary: arXiv:2611.27168v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We develop a continuum phenomenological theory for the kinetic arrest (KA) of a first-order phase transition (FOPT), taking the thermal and electric field-driven metal-insulator transition (MIT) in epitaxial V2O3 thin films as a prototype. By defining a coarse-grained mesoscopic order parameter representing the metallic volume fraction coupled to the primary structural monoclinic distortion, we formulate a Time-Dependent Ginzburg-Landau (TDGL) framework integrated with a non-local elastic interaction kernel and an Imry-Wortis quenched disorder landscape. We derive an explicit dynamic criterion for the kinetic arrest boundary TK(E) by analyzing the divergence of the intrinsic order-parameter relaxation time relative to experimental observation timescales. Our framework rigorously decouples the thermodynamic driving force from the kinetic activation barrier. We demonstrate that epitaxial substrate-induced clamping elevates local elastic barriers, pinning domain boundaries and stabilizing an arrested, inhomogeneous mosaic of metallic and insulating phases down to cryogenic temperatures. The simulated transformation kinetics exhibit an Avrami exponent suppression to values n < 1, reflecting slow, hindered domain-wall propagation. Furthermore, we examine the effect of an external electric field as an isothermal mechanism that lowers this kinetic barrier, providing a phenomenological description of threshold de-arrest and multi-level resistance states. We critically discuss this electronic barrier-lowering mechanism in comparison with electrothermal Joule heating, establish diagnostic criteria to distinguish them, and contextualize these non-equilibrium dynamics with related phenomena in disordered superconducting films.

item.title: Nonmonotonic Magnetic Correlations in Decorated Lieb-Lattice Anderson Models
item.description: arXiv:2611.27247v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The interplay between electronic correlations and lattice geometry can strongly modify the competition between magnetic correlations and local singlet formation in multiorbital Hamiltonians. Here we use determinant quantum Monte Car…
item.itunes:summary: arXiv:2611.27247v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The interplay between electronic correlations and lattice geometry can strongly modify the competition between magnetic correlations and local singlet formation in multiorbital Hamiltonians. Here we use determinant quantum Monte Carlo simulations to investigate two periodic Anderson-like models constructed by selectively hybridizing localized orbitals to the inequivalent sites of a Lieb lattice. The resulting geometries possess partially filled flat bands and different sublattice imbalances. We examine the evolution of local spin correlations and orbital-resolved magnetic structure factors as the hybridization is increased. Although correlations between hybridized orbitals evolve relatively smoothly toward local singlet formation, the longer-range magnetic correlations exhibit a striking nonmonotonic dependence on hybridization. In particular, we observe a pronounced suppression at intermediate hybridization followed by a substantial recovery on undecorated lattice sites. We discuss these results in relation to earlier studies of depleted periodic Anderson models and the constraints imposed by Lieb's theorem. Our findings illustrate how selective hybridization and flat-band structure can produce unusual redistributions of magnetic correlations in strongly interacting multiorbital systems.

item.title: Role of antisite disorder in dictating the Ising anisotropy and ferromagnetic ground state of NdGaSi
item.description: arXiv:2611.27334v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Single-ion anisotropy and exchange interactions together set the magnetic ground state of rare-earth intermetallics, yet the role of chemical disorder on the ligand sublattice remains little explored. Here, we show that Ga/Si antisi…
item.itunes:summary: arXiv:2611.27334v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Single-ion anisotropy and exchange interactions together set the magnetic ground state of rare-earth intermetallics, yet the role of chemical disorder on the ligand sublattice remains little explored. Here, we show that Ga/Si antisite disorder in NdGaSi stabilises the centrosymmetric $I4_1/amd$ structure and raises the Nd$^{3+}$ site symmetry to $D_{2d}$, which forbids all $m=\pm2$ Stevens operators in the crystalline electric field (CEF) Hamiltonian. Magnetization, specific heat, single-crystal neutron diffraction, and x-ray absorption spectroscopy establish the disordered structure and a collinear ferromagnetic order below $T_\mathrm{C}\approx11$~K with Ising anisotropy along $c$. A CEF analysis that fits the susceptibilities along both axes and the magnetic specific heat simultaneously yields a ground-state doublet that is $\sim97\%$ pure, in contrast to the strongly mixed ground state of the Al/Si-ordered NdAlSi ($C_{2v}$ site symmetry of Nd$^{3+}$). We argue that this ground-state purity makes the ordered moment rigid against the modulation due to frustrated exchange, selecting a $\mathbf{k}=0$ ferromagnet in NdGaSi instead of the incommensurate ferrimagnet of NdAlSi. Antisite disorder, thus, acts as a handle on CEF ground-state purity and can, thereby, select between fundamentally different magnetic ground states.

item.title: Lattice-geometry dependence of Type-I and Type-II magnetic flux responses in strongly correlated bosons
item.description: arXiv:2611.27749v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Superfluids and superconductors are classified into Type-I and Type-II according to their response to a magnetic flux, but this classification has hardly been addressed for lattice bosons under magnetic flux, where the Meissner and …
item.itunes:summary: arXiv:2611.27749v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Superfluids and superconductors are classified into Type-I and Type-II according to their response to a magnetic flux, but this classification has hardly been addressed for lattice bosons under magnetic flux, where the Meissner and vortex phases have been studied mostly in ladder geometries. Here, we study the flux response of the extended Bose-Hubbard model with nearest-neighbor interaction $V$ at half filling on square and triangular ladders with two to four legs by using the density-matrix renormalization group. On the square ladders, the vortex phase is confined to a region near $V=0$. At finite $V$, a magnetic flux-induced charge-density-wave (CDW) order replaces it, and the response becomes Type-I-like. In contrast, on the triangular ladders, the vortex phase persists over the whole range of $V$ studied, and the response remains Type-II-like. By extrapolating the ladder results to two dimensions, we argue that the Type-I or Type-II character of the flux response depends on the lattice geometry, which suggests a role of geometric frustration.

item.title: Magnetic-Field Response of a Hyperbolic Kitaev Spin Liquid
item.description: arXiv:2611.27819v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Hyperbolic geometry can give rise to Kitaev spin liquids with distinct flux structures and Majorana spectra, raising the question of how these fractionalized states respond beyond exactly solvable limits. We address this question on…
item.itunes:summary: arXiv:2611.27819v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Hyperbolic geometry can give rise to Kitaev spin liquids with distinct flux structures and Majorana spectra, raising the question of how these fractionalized states respond beyond exactly solvable limits. We address this question on the Kekul\'e-colored hyperbolic {8,3} lattice by developing an infinite projected entangled-pair-state approach with flux-resolved loop-gas initialization and geometry-adapted tensor-network contraction. Under uniform and staggered [111] magnetic fields, we find markedly different many-body responses. The uniform field induces a sharp change between competing variational branches at weak field, whereas the polarization and mean plaquette flux evolve over a much broader field range under the staggered field. Exchange-energy competition helps explain the different response scales, while third-order effective Majorana models in a fixed-flux background exhibit contrasting low-energy spectra. Our results connect the geometry-dependent fractionalized structure of a solvable hyperbolic spin liquid to its many-body response under physical perturbations that break flux conservation.

item.title: Quantum Many-Body Scars from Operator Size
item.description: arXiv:2611.27982v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We present a general construction of approximate many-body scar states in two copies of a system using a bilocal size interaction that couples one site to its partner on the other copy. For an uncoupled two-sided Hamiltonian whose t…
item.itunes:summary: arXiv:2611.27982v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We present a general construction of approximate many-body scar states in two copies of a system using a bilocal size interaction that couples one site to its partner on the other copy. For an uncoupled two-sided Hamiltonian whose terms have fixed size in an operator basis, we identify polynomially many Krylov basis states that it annihilates and that, in the thermodynamic limit, become concentrated on a single size sector. The size operator splits them into a tower of equally spaced levels that gives rise to coherent revivals characterized by collective oscillations of energy across the two copies. We provide a concrete realization of this construction in two copies of a general $q$-body nearest-neighbor spin chain, and the SYK model.

item.title: Topological phases protected by half-chiral symmetry
item.description: arXiv:2611.26693v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Chiral (or sublattice) symmetry describes bipartite systems such as the Su-Schrieffer-Heeger (SSH) chain where same-sublattice A-A and B-B hoppings are forbidden, enabling the protection of topological phases. Here we identify new…
item.itunes:summary: arXiv:2611.26693v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Chiral (or sublattice) symmetry describes bipartite systems such as the Su-Schrieffer-Heeger (SSH) chain where same-sublattice A-A and B-B hoppings are forbidden, enabling the protection of topological phases. Here we identify new topological phases protected by half-chiral symmetry wherein chiral symmetry is preserved on only one sublattice, as may occur with sublattice imbalance (e.g. graphene-hBN) or localized orbitals (e.g. zincblende). Unlike conventional symmetry operators described by group theory, half-chiral symmetry is an algebraic constraint on the sublattice-projected Hamiltonian such as $PHP=0$, requiring a new framework for topological protection. We develop such a framework, identifying real-space bulk topological invariants and corresponding topological boundary modes that stick to zero energy. In two dimensions we construct a half-chiral Kekule honeycomb model and show that its unusual higher-order topology protects a single zero-energy mode at a single corner.

item.title: Energy and Charge Transmission at Conformal Interfaces: Relations and Bounds
item.description: arXiv:2611.27002v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Symmetry constrains how independently energy and charge can pass through a conformal interface. For interfaces between Wess--Zumino--Witten (WZW) models $G_{k_L}$ and $G_{k_R}$ preserving the diagonal affine algebra, we derive an …
item.itunes:summary: arXiv:2611.27002v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Symmetry constrains how independently energy and charge can pass through a conformal interface. For interfaces between Wess--Zumino--Witten (WZW) models $G_{k_L}$ and $G_{k_R}$ preserving the diagonal affine algebra, we derive an exact relation between the energy and charge transmission coefficients, $c_{LR}=2(\dim G)k_{LR}/(k_L+k_R+2h^\vee)$. Together with positivity of outgoing energy, this relation excludes complete energy transmission at unequal levels. With additional bulk degrees of freedom, the equality is replaced by bounds controlled by the coset central charges. Complete transmission from a lower-level WZW model then imposes a lower bound on the coset central charge on the other side. In linear response, the relation fixes the ratio of thermal to charge conductance to the harmonic mean of the two bulk ratios, independently of the interface, while coset sectors bound the thermal conductance at fixed charge conductance. This interface-independent ratio is a generalized Wiedemann--Franz law for conformal interfaces between WZW models. The charge transmission coefficient $k_{LR}$ also governs equilibrium charge fluctuations and fixes the leading quadratic dependence of the boundary-condition-changing operator's scaling dimension on the rotation angle.

item.title: Growth and anisotropic directional dependent transport properties of Altermagnetic CrSb
item.description: arXiv:2611.27072v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: CrSb is a metallic altermagnet exhibiting large momentum-dependent spin splitting and antifer- romagnetic ordering well above room temperature. Although its electronic and magnetotransport properties have attracted considerable at…
item.itunes:summary: arXiv:2611.27072v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: CrSb is a metallic altermagnet exhibiting large momentum-dependent spin splitting and antifer- romagnetic ordering well above room temperature. Although its electronic and magnetotransport properties have attracted considerable attention, a systematic comparison of crystals prepared us- ing different growth methods remains limited. Here we investigate the structural, magnetic, and anisotropic transport properties of CrSb single crystals grown by Sb(self)-flux, Bi flux, and chem- ical vapor transport (CVT). Each of these growth reveals distinct crystal morphologies. Magne- tization measurements exhibit broadly consistent antiferromagnetic responses, with an additional low-temperature contribution observed in Bi-flux-grown crystals. All samples display metallic resis- tivity and positive, nonsaturating magnetoresistance up to 9 T. Sb-flux- and CVT-grown crystals exhibit comparable residual resistivity ratios and magnetoresistance, whereas Bi-flux-grown crys- tals show enhanced residual resistivity and a substantially reduced magnetoresistance, consistent with stronger carrier scattering. Hall measurements reveal a pronounced dependence on the field- current configuration, including nonlinear field dependence and opposite Hall polarities for different crystallographic orientations. These results establish the reproducibility of anisotropic magneto- transport across distinct growth routes while highlighting the sensitivity of carrier scattering to crystal-growth conditions. Our findings provide a comparative framework for selecting CrSb single crystals for orientation-dependent transport and spintronic investigations.

item.title: Pairing and modular: Generalized electrons and quasiholes inside the $\boxtimes$ of topological orders
item.description: arXiv:2611.27378v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study the relationship between the pair creation mechanism in physics and the pairing ($\boxtimes_{\mathbf{A}_{\text{ub}}}$) in mathematics, focusing on the modular and algebraic properties. We provide a way to couple two topol…
item.itunes:summary: arXiv:2611.27378v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study the relationship between the pair creation mechanism in physics and the pairing ($\boxtimes_{\mathbf{A}_{\text{ub}}}$) in mathematics, focusing on the modular and algebraic properties. We provide a way to couple two topologically ordered systems, $\mathbf{A}$ and $\mathbf{A'}$ sharing the common (non-group-like) structure $\mathbf{A}_{\text{ub}}=\overline{\mathbf{A'}_{\text{ub}}}$, through the nonabelian anyon analog of the pair creation mechanism denoted as $\mathbf{A}_{\text{ub},\boxtimes}=\mathbf{A}_{\text{ub}}\boxtimes \mathbf{A'}_{\text{ub}}$. We identify $\mathbf{A}_{\text{ub},\boxtimes}$ as the generalized version of electron operators in general topological orders or hidden current with (half-)integer spin involving the conformal embeddings. We provide a way to construct $\mathbf{A}_{\text{ub},\boxtimes}$ as the hidden topological operator and identify $\mathbf{A}\boxtimes_{\mathbf{A}_{\text{ub}}}\mathbf{A'}$, a general class of topoloical orders, as the $\mathbf{A}_{\text{ub},\boxtimes}$-extended symmetry topological field theory. We also conjecture a series of underlying (unexplored) modular invariants, connecting the conformal embedding and the pairing.

item.title: Quantum computing for gearing down complex many-fermion problems
item.description: arXiv:2611.27402v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Quantum computing unlocks exciting opportunities to extend first-principles calculations of quantum many-body systems beyond classical computing limits. Despite advances in algorithms and proof-of-principle experiments, large-scal…
item.itunes:summary: arXiv:2611.27402v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Quantum computing unlocks exciting opportunities to extend first-principles calculations of quantum many-body systems beyond classical computing limits. Despite advances in algorithms and proof-of-principle experiments, large-scale {\it ab initio} calculations on noisy intermediate-scale quantum (NISQ) devices remain challenging. We introduce a quantum-classical framework that identifies compact single-particle bases to bring otherwise intractable many-fermion problems within classical reach while preserving an accurate ground-state description. We develop an efficient adaptive search scheme driven by simulated annealing that jointly optimizes natural-orbital-guided transformations and active-space selections. A quantum-assisted ground-state estimator provides search guidance using low-depth circuits and relaxed accuracy requirements, making the framework promising for NISQ devices. We demonstrate the framework's applicability for the nuclear structure of the oxygen isotopes. Our framework opens a new route to tackling complex {\it ab initio} many-fermion problems across disciplines through quantum-assisted basis reduction.

item.title: Comparing weakly interacting and free quantum dynamics locally
item.description: arXiv:2611.27707v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Lieb-Robinson bounds (LRBs) have become a standard tool for perturbative results in quantum many-body physics, including gap stability and many-body adiabatic theory. Here, we use LRBs to locally approximate weakly interacting man…
item.itunes:summary: arXiv:2611.27707v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Lieb-Robinson bounds (LRBs) have become a standard tool for perturbative results in quantum many-body physics, including gap stability and many-body adiabatic theory. Here, we use LRBs to locally approximate weakly interacting many-body dynamics with one-body dynamics on large, perturbative time scales. This allows us to use one-body transport results to establish the expected many-body transport behavior on finite time scales in the following two illustrative settings: (i) We prove quantum diffusion, as quantified by a certain operator spreading diagnostic, in weakly interacting and weakly disordered Fermi systems in dimensions $D\geq2$ on large finite time scales based on the non-interacting diffusion result of Black, Drogin, and Hern\'andez [arXiv:2506.06468]. (ii) We show for Fermi-Hubbard models with initially low spin-down density, that all local multi-time spin-up correlation functions are approximated by their free counterparts. In particular, we obtain an OTOC (out-of-time-ordered correlator) counterpart to the patterns of short-time entanglement related to lattice path counts observed numerically by Bippus et al. [Phys. Rev. B 113, 035152 (2026)].

item.title: Solving fermionic sign problems with physics-informed kernels
item.description: arXiv:2611.27768v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We extend the generative sampling approach with physics-informed kernels (PIKs) [1,2] to a general class of physics systems with complex distributions and a structure also encountered in fermionic systems. The resolution of sign p…
item.itunes:summary: arXiv:2611.27768v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We extend the generative sampling approach with physics-informed kernels (PIKs) [1,2] to a general class of physics systems with complex distributions and a structure also encountered in fermionic systems. The resolution of sign problems of generic weighted sums of complex Gau{\ss}ian distributions with the PIK approach is central to this application. In a first step, PIKs map a real normal distribution to such a weighted sum, and this procedure is called the PIKfan. The PIKfan has the sampling cost of a real normal distribution. In a second step, this weighted sum is evolved with a second PIK into the distribution of the theory at hand. In combination, we reduce the sampling task for a general class of complex systems to a Gau{\ss}ian one, and the main computational task is that of computing the PIK. We illustrate the approach with the one-site Hubbard model at arbitrary chemical potential and with $\phi^4$-deformed extensions of it.

item.title: Optimised 8th-Order Trotter-Suzuki Schemes for Quantum Simulation
item.description: arXiv:2611.27896v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Simulating quantum dynamics in many-body systems is one of the most promising applications of quantum computers. Product formulas are a natural choice for this task, since they map directly onto quantum gates, and increasing their…
item.itunes:summary: arXiv:2611.27896v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Simulating quantum dynamics in many-body systems is one of the most promising applications of quantum computers. Product formulas are a natural choice for this task, since they map directly onto quantum gates, and increasing their order $n$ could lead to reduced gate depths, provided the parameters are chosen efficiently. So far, schemes beyond $6^{\textrm{th}}$ order have only been built as compositions of second-order schemes, while more general product formulas are known only up to $6^{\textrm{th}}$ order. In this work, we extend our optimisation framework to order $n = 8$, and find both more efficient compositions and the first $8^{\textrm{th}}$ order general schemes. Our formulas improve on the theoretical efficiency of the state-of-the-art schemes by Morales et al and we recommend two schemes explicitly. In simulations of the Heisenberg XZ chain one of our recommended schemes always outperforms those by Morales et al, though it is not always the same scheme that performs best. More generally, we observe that for Hamiltonians split into many non-commuting operators the uniformity of a Trotter decomposition becomes the main indicator of a scheme's performance. To assess the schemes' use on quantum hardware, we simulate noisy circuits with our new Qiskit plugin qiskit-omelyan. At current noise levels, the Leapfrog scheme remains the best choice, but as noise rates decrease toward fault tolerance, our recommended schemes become competitive.

item.title: Structure and relaxation of long-lived odd-parity modes in two-dimensional Fermi liquids
item.description: arXiv:2611.27980v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: In two-dimensional Fermi liquids, odd-parity deformations of the Fermi surface relax anomalously slowly at a rate $\sim T^4$, where $T$ is the temperature. However, the leading-logarithmic prediction for the magnitude of this rate…
item.itunes:summary: arXiv:2611.27980v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: In two-dimensional Fermi liquids, odd-parity deformations of the Fermi surface relax anomalously slowly at a rate $\sim T^4$, where $T$ is the temperature. However, the leading-logarithmic prediction for the magnitude of this rate $\sim m^4 \ln m$, where $m$ is an angular harmonic index, exceeds exact-diagonalization results and the $\ln m$ scaling is not observed. We resolve this discrepancy by evaluating the 2D Fermi-liquid collision integral for general regular isotropic potentials to leading order in $T/T_F$, including the nonlogarithmic term beyond the $\ln(T_F/T)$ term. We find that the local temperature modulation of the odd mode, which we call the thermal dressing, suppresses relaxation by collinear scattering, with residual relaxation set by large-angle scattering. Such large-angle processes give corrections of order $\ln m/\ln(T_F/T)$ that are not small and must be resummed. We benchmark our results against exact-diagonalization calculations for constant interactions and find agreement over a range $m^2 T/T_F \lesssim 0.4$, and we provide closed-form results for the slowest odd-mode relaxation rate of a spin-polarized dipolar gas.

item.title: Thermopower overshoot from collinear scattering in two-dimensional Fermi liquids
item.description: arXiv:2611.27981v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Electron transport is typically described in terms of relaxation times, which measure how quickly Fermi-surface deformations decay. We show here that the thermopower of a two-dimensional Fermi liquid instead probes the structure o…
item.itunes:summary: arXiv:2611.27981v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Electron transport is typically described in terms of relaxation times, which measure how quickly Fermi-surface deformations decay. We show here that the thermopower of a two-dimensional Fermi liquid instead probes the structure of these deformations in the form of their local temperature change, which we call the thermal dressing. This structure leads to an overshoot of the thermopower over its hydrodynamic value $- s/(ne)$ with increasing wave vector, before it falls to half that value in the ballistic limit. At low temperatures, the excess thermopower does not have the linear-in-temperature scaling expected of a Fermi liquid, but decreases only logarithmically as $1/\ln(T_F/T)$ at optimal wave vector. The overshoot is caused by collinear scattering, which redistributes energy over the Fermi surface and induces the thermal dressing, the strength of which grows with the angular harmonic index $m$ of the deformation. In contrast to tomographic effects in the charge conductivity, this overshoot does not rely on an odd-even effect in quasiparticle lifetimes and defines a distinct thermographic transport regime. The thermopower overshoot survives realistic disorder and should be detectable in a thermocouple with high-mobility samples.

item.title: Dynamics and stability of U(1) spin liquids beyond mean-field theory: Triangular-lattice $J_1$-$J_2$ Heisenberg model
item.description: arXiv:2503.13831v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Quantum spin liquids (QSLs) are long-range entangled phases of frustrated magnets exhibiting fractionalised spin excitations. In two dimensions, there is limited analytical understanding of their excitation spectra beyond parton…
item.itunes:summary: arXiv:2503.13831v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Quantum spin liquids (QSLs) are long-range entangled phases of frustrated magnets exhibiting fractionalised spin excitations. In two dimensions, there is limited analytical understanding of their excitation spectra beyond parton mean-field theories, which fail to capture many features of the finite frequency dynamical response. We use a self-consistent mean-field theory combined with the random phase approximation (RPA) for the $J_1$-$J_2$ Heisenberg model on the triangular lattice to describe the strong spinon-spinon interactions of the U(1) Dirac QSL. We obtain quantitative results for the dynamical spin structure factor and phase diagram compatible with comprehensive numerical efforts. We show the continuum response at the Brillouin zone corners is described by a spinon-exciton hybridised with monopole gauge excitations. We further show that the transition from the QSL to 120-degree coplanar order is in the QED$_3$ O(3)-GN universality class. We extend the method to chiral QSLs and XXZ anisotropy, and discuss its broad range of applicability to other models and for describing inelastic neutron scattering experiments in KYbSe$_2$.

item.title: Probing Topological Phases in a Strongly Correlated Ladder Model via Entanglement
item.description: arXiv:2510.26713v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: This work examines the interplay of band topology and interactions in a spinless two-leg ladder with $p$-wave-like inter-orbital hybridization. In the non-interacting limit, the model hosts three topologically distinct insulatin…
item.itunes:summary: arXiv:2510.26713v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: This work examines the interplay of band topology and interactions in a spinless two-leg ladder with $p$-wave-like inter-orbital hybridization. In the non-interacting limit, the model hosts three topologically distinct insulating phases, denoted by $A$, $B$, and $C$. Combining density-matrix renormalization group calculations with low-energy theories of the critical lines yields the interacting phase diagram for an inter-orbital density-density interaction. The $A$-$C$ boundary contains two Dirac valleys and has central charge $c=2$ in the free theory. In the presence of interaction, the exact reflection symmetry pins the $A$-$C$ boundary to its free-theory location, while the critical theory evolves to $c=1$ and the edge entanglement entropy changes from $2\ln 2$ to $\ln 2$. The $B$-$C$ boundary contains a single Dirac mode and shifts quadratically with interaction strength through second-order self-energy corrections involving virtual heavy modes, while retaining its $c=1$ critical structure. Charge conservation and antiunitary many-body chiral symmetry give an interacting $\mathbb{Z}_4$ classification. This distinguishes the two interacting topological phases despite their identical lowest entanglement-spectrum degeneracy. The boundary response is governed by the symmetry and operator content of its critical theory and the symmetry-protected topology of the adjoining phases.

item.title: Evidence for itinerant electron-local moment interaction in Li-doped $\alpha$-MnTe
item.description: arXiv:2512.00747v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We use inelastic neutron scattering (INS) and angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy (ARPES) to study the impact of Li doping on the semiconducting altermagnet $\alpha$-MnTe. Introducing Li reorients the ordered moment direct…
item.itunes:summary: arXiv:2512.00747v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We use inelastic neutron scattering (INS) and angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy (ARPES) to study the impact of Li doping on the semiconducting altermagnet $\alpha$-MnTe. Introducing Li reorients the ordered moment direction from in-plane to out-of-plane and increases the density of itinerant carriers. While our ARPES measurements do not indicate any notable doping-induced changes in the electronic band structure or the magnitude of the altermagnetic band splitting, our INS measurements reveal an abrupt doping-induced decrease in the spin-wave lifetime near the zone boundary at high energies. This finding is consistent with a new magnon decay channel driven by subtle, doping-induced changes in the band structure and enhanced interactions between Mn$^{2+}$ local moments and itinerant electrons. By extracting the local dynamic susceptibility from INS spectra and applying the total moment sum rule, we find that both undoped and Li-doped $\alpha$-MnTe exhibit a nearly full expected Mn$^{2+}$ local moment of $\approx5.9~\mu_\mathrm{B}$ with $S=5/2$. These findings suggest that $\alpha$-MnTe hosts robust local-moment altermagnetism which shows a breakdown at high energies upon addition of itinerant carriers, highlighting the importance of carrier-spin coupling in magneto-transport and spin dynamics of altermagnets, even in the dilute-carrier limit.

item.title: Lowering the temperature of two-dimensional fermionic tensor networks with cluster expansions
item.description: arXiv:2602.22113v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Representing the time-evolution operator as a tensor network constitutes a key ingredient in several algorithms for studying quantum lattice systems at finite temperature or in a non-equilibrium setting. For a Hamiltonian compos…
item.itunes:summary: arXiv:2602.22113v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Representing the time-evolution operator as a tensor network constitutes a key ingredient in several algorithms for studying quantum lattice systems at finite temperature or in a non-equilibrium setting. For a Hamiltonian composed of strictly short-ranged interactions, the Suzuki-Trotter decomposition is the main technique for obtaining such a representation. In [B.~Vanhecke, L.~Vanderstraeten and F.~Verstraete, Physical Review A, L020402 (2021)], an alternative strategy, the cluster expansion, was introduced. This approach naturally preserves internal and lattice symmetries and can more easily be extended to higher-order representations or longer-ranged interactions. We extend the cluster expansion to two-dimensional fermionic systems, and employ it to construct projected entangled-pair operator (PEPO) approximations of Gibbs states. We also discuss and benchmark different truncation schemes for multiplying layers of PEPOs together. Applying the resulting framework to a two-dimensional spinless fermion model with attractive interactions, we resolve a clear phase boundary at finite temperature.

item.title: Symmetry-Resolved Spectral Weight Reveals Charge Localization in Correlated Insulator
item.description: arXiv:2603.11879v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Can crystalline symmetry reveal where charge localizes in a strongly correlated insulator? We show that occupied symmetry-resolved spectral weights of the exact electronic Green's function define effective atomic limits. In an i…
item.itunes:summary: arXiv:2603.11879v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Can crystalline symmetry reveal where charge localizes in a strongly correlated insulator? We show that occupied symmetry-resolved spectral weights of the exact electronic Green's function define effective atomic limits. In an interacting Su-Schrieffer-Heeger chain, their displacement tracks the spin-resolved many-body polarization across distinct insulating phases. A quantum metric of the one-body reduced density matrix provides a complementary geometric characterization. Our results extend real-space symmetry analysis beyond occupied-band projectors.

item.title: Type-IV 't Hooft Anomalies on the Lattice: Emergent Higher-Categorical Symmetries and Applications to LSM Systems
item.description: arXiv:2604.02856v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: 't Hooft anomalies impose fundamental constraints on quantum matter and often lead to emergent symmetry structures upon gauging. We analyze a lattice model with four global symmetries realizing a mixed anomaly described by $\sim…
item.itunes:summary: arXiv:2604.02856v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: 't Hooft anomalies impose fundamental constraints on quantum matter and often lead to emergent symmetry structures upon gauging. We analyze a lattice model with four global symmetries realizing a mixed anomaly described by $\sim a_1\wedge a_2\wedge a_3\wedge a_4$, where the $a_i$ denote background gauge fields for the global symmetries. Through explicit lattice gauging, we demonstrate the emergence of higher symmetry structures, including 2-group, non-invertible, and higher fusion categorical symmetries. We also provide a field theoretical understanding of these results. Applying this framework to systems with Lieb-Schultz-Mattis anomalies, obtained by promoting part of the internal symmetries to translational symmetries, we demonstrate that modulated (dipole) symmetries and non-invertible translation symmetry arise as direct counterparts of those in systems with purely internal type-IV anomalies. Importantly, we uncover a qualitatively new feature absent in previously studied modulated symmetries and non-invertible translation: their realization can become intrinsically defect-dependent. In particular, the emergent symmetry structure changes depending on whether symmetry defects are present. This work establishes a concrete lattice realization of mixed anomalies and reveals a rich structure of emergent symmetries, thereby clarifying their role in constraining quantum phases of matter.

item.title: Electronic structure, quasiparticle renormalizations, and magnetic correlations in the alternating single-layer bilayer nickelate La$_5$Ni$_3$O$_{11}$
item.description: arXiv:2604.26627v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Using DFT+DMFT we study the electronic structure and magnetic correlations in the recently discovered alternating single-layer bilayer Ruddlesden-Popper nickelate La$_5$Ni$_3$O$_{11}$ (1212-LNO). Our results exhibit qualitative …
item.itunes:summary: arXiv:2604.26627v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Using DFT+DMFT we study the electronic structure and magnetic correlations in the recently discovered alternating single-layer bilayer Ruddlesden-Popper nickelate La$_5$Ni$_3$O$_{11}$ (1212-LNO). Our results exhibit qualitative differences for the structurally distinct single-layer and bilayer Ni ions, implying the importance of confinement and orbital-dependent correlations. The Ni $e_g$ states originating from the bilayer Ni ions form strongly renormalized quasiparticle bands with a large enhancement factor $m^*/m \sim 3.5$ and 4.2 for the Ni $x^2-y^2$ and $3z^2-r^2$ orbitals. Moreover, the $e_g$ states of the single-layer Ni ions exhibit an orbital-selective Mott insulating state, with a narrow energy gap for the Ni $3z^2-r^2$ states and metallic, strongly non-Fermi-liquid Ni $x^2-y^2$ ones. Our analysis of magnetic correlations suggests the formation of intertwined spin and charge density wave stripes in the bilayer NiO$_6$ slab, in close similarity to the double-layer material. We identify two major instabilities: a leading one associated with a propagating wave vector ${\bf Q}=(\frac{1}{3},\frac{1}{3})$ ("up-down-0" spin pattern or "$d^8$-$d^8$-$d^8\underline{L}$'' charge-density wave with Ni $d^8\underline{L}$ ions bonded in an interlayer spin polaron), competing with $(\frac{1}{4},\frac{1}{4})$ ("up-up-down-down") stripe state. The single-layer Ni $3d$ electrons exhibit an instability toward the N\'eel magnetic state. Under pressure, 1212-LNO undergoes an orbital-selective Mott insulator-to-metal transition, associated with metallization of the single-layer Ni $e_g$ states. The single-layer Ni $e_g$ bands exhibit non-Fermi-liquid behavior with strongly incoherent spectral weights near $E_F$. We note that correlation effects result in a crossover from single-layer (as obtained within DFT) to double-layer dominated magnetic correlations.

item.title: Deconfined criticality between an antiferromagnetic insulator and a nodal d-wave superconductor: a quantum Monte Carlo study
item.description: arXiv:2607.00762v5 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We present a quantum Monte Carlo study of the transition between the insulating N\'eel state and the nodal $d$-wave superconductor on the square lattice at half-filling. We access a regime of frustrated magnetic order without a …
item.itunes:summary: arXiv:2607.00762v5 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We present a quantum Monte Carlo study of the transition between the insulating N\'eel state and the nodal $d$-wave superconductor on the square lattice at half-filling. We access a regime of frustrated magnetic order without a sign problem using a parton representation of the electron in terms of fermionic spinons and bosonic chargons. Both partons move in a background $\pi$-flux (so the electron experiences no net flux) and are coupled to a quantum fluctuating SU(2) lattice gauge field. In contrast to earlier studies directly on the electronic degrees of freedom, we find evidence for a second-order deconfined quantum phase transition at which both the N\'eel and $d$-wave superconductivity orders vanish continuously. We compute correlators of the spinon-chargon composite with the same quantum numbers as the electron: we find a gapless Dirac dispersion inside the $d$-wave superconductor, turning into a gapped dispersion in the antiferromagnet.

item.title: Local moment magnon spectrum in conduction electron tunnelling
item.description: arXiv:2607.05858v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The surface tunnelling spectrum of a dual system consisting of localised moments with antiferromagnetic order coupled to conduction electrons by on-site exchange interaction is investigated. In the static approximation of the lo…
item.itunes:summary: arXiv:2607.05858v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The surface tunnelling spectrum of a dual system consisting of localised moments with antiferromagnetic order coupled to conduction electrons by on-site exchange interaction is investigated. In the static approximation of the local moment order it is known that magnetic band reconstruction leads to an anomalous tunnelling spectrum at the magnetic ordering vector of local moments although the latter cannot contribute directly. In this work we consider dynamic effects by including the scattering of conduction electrons from the local moment magnon excitations. They lead to self energies and renormalisation of conduction states which in turn appreciably modify the tunnelling spectrum beyond the influence of static order, interpreted as the appearance of magnon sidebands.

item.title: Non-Equilibrium Instantaneous Approximation and Dipole Forbidden d-d Transitions
item.description: arXiv:2608.16219v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Time- and angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy provides direct access to pump-induced changes in the electronic structure of correlated materials, but its theoretical description generally requires computationally demanding…
item.itunes:summary: arXiv:2608.16219v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Time- and angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy provides direct access to pump-induced changes in the electronic structure of correlated materials, but its theoretical description generally requires computationally demanding two-time non-equilibrium calculations. We introduce an instantaneous approximation for pump-driven correlated systems, based on a separation between the rapid decay of the Green's functions in the relative time variable and their slower evolution in the average time. Combined with a one-shot dynamical mean-field construction at the Hubbard I level, the method incorporates the driven dynamics of the local correlated shell into the lattice Green's function while retaining momentum resolution. We also derive an effective coupling for nominally dipole-forbidden d-d excitations. It arises from a dipole-allowed d-p transition followed by p-d hybridization; beyond the instantaneous limit, the same process produces an energy-dependent vertex correction to the optical response. As a proof of principle, we apply the framework to paramagnetic and antiferromagnetic FePS3, using a density-functional theory derived tight-binding model together with a supercell unfolding procedure. The calculated momentum-resolved spectra reproduce the main qualitative features observed after excitation of the first and second d-d transitions in recent time-resolved photoemission experiments.

item.title: Spin Space Symmetry Without Spin Space Groups
item.description: arXiv:2610.37770v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Spin space groups provide a complete symmetry classification of magnetic structures in the non-relativistic limit. Each spin space group with a given parent space group is specified, up to spin-only symmetries, by a real represe…
item.itunes:summary: arXiv:2610.37770v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Spin space groups provide a complete symmetry classification of magnetic structures in the non-relativistic limit. Each spin space group with a given parent space group is specified, up to spin-only symmetries, by a real representation of that space group acting in spin space. We argue that working directly with this representation not only avoids the construction and identification of the group, but also organizes and simplifies the resulting symmetry constraints on allowed responses. The presence or absence of magnetic compensation, piezomagnetism, spin and charge transport, the Edelstein effect, and momentum-space spin textures becomes an ordinary problem in the representation theory of space groups. The conditions reduce to overlaps between the three exterior powers of the defining representation and multipole representations of the point group. Several physically distinct responses then reduce to the same condition: a $p$-wave spin texture and the time-even Edelstein effect are allowed together, as are piezomagnetism and a $d$-wave spin texture in compensated order. The wave-vector content of the exterior powers gives a hierarchy of selection rules: depending on the power, a uniform response requires one, two, or three ordering wave vectors to sum to a reciprocal lattice vector. A non-relativistic anomalous Hall effect in compensated order at zero wave vector requires a defining representation built from three one-dimensional irreducible representations, a purely odd-parity spin texture requires a pair of nonzero ordering wave vectors that cancel, and coplanar order at nonzero wave vector in the interior of the Brillouin zone is always a $p$-wave magnet. We illustrate the approach with collinear, coplanar and non-coplanar magnets, and discuss extensions to magnetic space groups, connections to Landau theories of collinear order, and the characterization of odd-parity magnets.
